speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I am Dr. Agent; I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin our assessment, how many weeks pregnant was the mother when you were born, and was there any involvement of the umbilical cord or placenta during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity.

The history of 33-week gestation and immediate onset of respiratory distress two hours after birth is highly characteristic of RDS. Given the lack of prenatal care and early prematurity, surfactant deficiency is the primary concern. We can proceed with confirmation if needed, but the clinical picture is classic.

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Gas_Analysis (to check pH, pCO2, and pO2).
REQUEST TEST: Chest_XRay (to look for ground-glass opacity).
